reuse.why: Builds every step on the existing shared getScheduledAmount and reuses getApproxNumberThreshold, routing the API's expectedAmount and all server/client consumers through it.

duplication.why: Removes five inline midpoint copies (forecast, updateActions, postTransactionForSchedule, preview, schedule-template) in favour of the one helper; no new duplication.

placement.why: The planning rule lives in shared/schedules.ts; api-models only maps the field and callers forward their operator.

scope.why: Edits serve the four steps; switching the client list/balance displays to the operator-aware amount is a consequence of the shared rule rather than a stray change, and three release notes are slightly redundant.

maintainability.why: One helper owns missing/single/range/approx; inserting op positionally before the existing inverse flag makes boolean-at-position-3 calls easy to misuse, and useScheduleEdit calls still omit the op.

bypasses_abstraction.where: All amount resolution goes through getScheduledAmount after the change.

abstraction_drift.where: getScheduledAmount gains an op parameter (ahead of inverse) and an isapprox branch in getPlannedAmount; the step-4 rule change is a one-line edit inside the helper, and no call site re-implements it.
